speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and a headache. To help me understand the timeline and severity of your condition, have you noticed any joint pain or muscle aches recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Human Herpesvirus 6 or 7). The classic presentation of a one-week prodrome of fever, rhinorrhea, and headache followed by the appearance of a rash after the fever breaks (though your history notes the rash starting earlier, the specific detail of a facial rash sparing the perioral area in an 11-year-old is highly suggestive of secondary syphilis or measles; however, given the "low-grade" fever and specific rash description, I must clarify the fever pattern. Did the fever resolve completely before the rash appeared, or did it persist? Also, has there been any exposure to measles or rubella contacts recently?
